previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a left chest portacath was admitted with acute right wrist and hip pain. She was found to have MSSA bacteremia, likely originating from her portacath. The right wrist showed signs of septic tenosynovitis, confirmed by purulence and positive cultures after surgical washout. The hip joint aspiration was negative, and MRI showed no abscess or fracture, though pain persisted. She also developed C. difficile colitis during admission, requiring oral vancomycin and metronidazole. Her portacath was retained with antibiotic locks due to difficult vascular access. Insulin was uptitrated for hyperglycemia, and she completed dialysis sessions. She improved clinically, with resolving infection and pain, and was discharged home on a six-week course of IV cefazolin, oral metronidazole, and portacath antibiotic locks, with follow-up planned.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is ___ lady w/ difficult to control DM1, ESRD on 
___ HD, recurrent gastroparesis, and recent admission for 
MSSA bacteremia c/b c. difficile admitted with recurrent 
gastroparesis flare.
  
# Gastroparesis flare:  
Patient with history of numerous admissions for similar 
complaints, attributed to diabetic gastroparesis. Her symptoms 
on admission were c/w prior flares. Possible triggers include 
hyperglycemia (FSG 600s on admission) and volume overload with 
bowel edema (about 7kg above her dry weight on admission). Pt. 
was placed on bowel rest, underwent two HD sessions with 
significant fluid removal, and had mildly better glucose 
control.  Her symptoms improved significantly and by discharge 
she was tolerating a full diet without difficulties.

# Diabetes mellitus, type 1: 
Pt. with long history of extremely difficult to control type 1 
diabetes.  Complications include nephropathy and gastroparesis.  
Pt. was continued on home insulin with moderate control.

# MSSA bacteremia: Presumed due to indwelling portacath. 
Bacteremia complicated by recent admission for polyarticular 
septic arthritis.  Pt. seen by orthopedics who removed sutures 
from right wrist and reported that it was healing well.  Hip 
pain had resolved prior to admission, and pt. was ambulating 
without difficulty.  Pt. was continued on cefazolin post-HD for 
6 weeks total ending ___ and on vancomycin-sodium citrate 
locks to port daily and prn port access for 4 weeks total ending 
___.
  
# C diff infection: Patient was continued on oral metronidazole 
to complete ___nding ___ in conjunction with 
end of cefazolin.

Pt was continued on HD ___ with one additional session for 
extra volume removal. She was continued on a renal diet and home 
Ca, Vit D, nephrocaps, sevelamer, and lasix. 

# HTN:

control.
